claims.text: The inspected paper states that for \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the ideal \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by each of \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}. \] [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]

864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .

claims.text: In the inclusion special case \(t=r\) or \(t=s\), the paper compares its second family with the generators of Gasharov–Reiner (GR02); for \(t=s\), it has \(i=b=1\), \(j=r-s+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-1,s-1)\), and obtains the first \(\min(n-r,s)\) GR02 generators. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 893-933]

893: Example 4.9 .
894: We examine the special case where the bigrassmannian
895: v:=v_{r,s,t,n} has t equal to r or s, so that the Schubert condition C_{r,s,t}
896: in 4.1 becomes an inclusion
897: V_{r}\subseteq{\mathbb{C}}^{s} or V_{r}\supseteq{\mathbb{C}}^{s}.
898: Schubert varieties X_{w} in type A for which
899: all Schubert conditions on X_{w} take one of these two forms
900: were called Schubert varieties defined by inclusions in
901: [ GR02 ] . That paper gave a presentation for the cohomology
902: containing
903: \bullet
904: for each inclusion condition V_{r}\supseteq{\mathbb{C}}^{s},
905: a set of s generators for J_{v} of the form
906: (4.7)
907: \{e_{m}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{r})\}_{m=r-s+1,r-s+2,\ldots,r},
908: \bullet
909: and for each inclusion condition V_{r}\subseteq{\mathbb{C}}^{s},
910: a set of r generators for J_{v} of the form
911: (4.8)
912: \{e_{m}(x_{r}+1,\ldots,x_{n})\}_{m=s-r+1,s-r+2,\ldots,n-r}.
913: We compare this with the presentation for J_{v}
914: in Theorem 4.8 ,
915: say for the inclusion conditions of the form
916: V_{r}\supseteq{\mathbb{C}}^{s}, and using the
917: generators given in ( 4.6 ).
918: Since t=s, one has
919: \displaystyle i
920: \displaystyle=s-t+1=1
921: \displaystyle j
922: \displaystyle=r-s+1
923: \displaystyle b
924: \displaystyle=\min(i,j)=i=1
925: \displaystyle a
926: \displaystyle=\min(n-r-1,s-1)
927: Hence ( 4.6 ) says
928: that J_{v} is generated by the set of a+1 Schur functions
929: \{s_{\mu}:1^{r-s+1}\subseteq\mu\subseteq 1^{a+r-s+1}\}=\{e_{m}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{r})\}_{m=r-s+1,r-s+2,\ldots,a+r-s+1}
930: which is exactly the first a+1=\min(n-r,s) out of the s generators
931: listed in ( 4.7 ). Hence Theorem 4.8
932: provides a dramatic reduction in the size of the
933: generating set for J_{v} whenever n-r is small compared to s.

67: The above facts lead to an a priori presentation
68: for H^{\star}(X_{w}); see also [ C92 , Cor. 4.4] and
69: [ GR02 , Prop. 2.1] : The Schubert variety X_{w} is the
70: union of the Schubert cells X_{u}^{\circ} for which u\leq w in the
71: (strong) Bruhat order ; hence it inherits a cell decomposition
72: from the flag variety. Consequently, the map on cohomology
73: H^{\star}(G/B)\rightarrow H^{\star}(X_{w})
74: induced by including X_{w}\hookrightarrow G/B is surjective
75: with kernel
76: (1.2)
77: I_{w}:=\Bbbk\text{-span of }\{\sigma_{u}:u\not\leq w\}.
78: This gives rise to presentations
79: (1.3)
80: \displaystyle H^{\star}(X_{w})
81: \displaystyle\cong H^{\star}(G/B)/I_{w}
82: \displaystyle\text{ working over }{\mathbb{Z}}
83: \displaystyle\cong\Bbbk[V]/\left(I_{w}+\Bbbk[V]^{W}_{+}\right)
84: \displaystyle\text{ working over }\Bbbk.
85: This presentation ( 1.3 ) involves a generating set ( 1.2 )
86: for I_{w} with at most |W| generators. However, this generating set
87: for I_{w} is wasteful in that it not only generates I_{w} as an ideal but
88: actually spans it \Bbbk- linearly within H^{\star}(G/B).
89: Therefore, a basic question is to request more efficient generating
90: sets for I_{w}. For type A_{n-1}, earlier work
91: [ GR02 ] reduced the |W|=n! upper bound on the number
92: of generators for I_{w} to a polynomial bound of n^{2} for the class
93: of Schubert varieties X_{w} defined by inclusions ; this class
94: includes all smooth X_{w}. Moreover, for a certain subclass of smooth
95: Schubert varieties X_{w} considered originally by Ding
96: [ D97 , D01 ] , they gave a smaller generating set for these I_{w}
97: having only n generators. This latter result was applied in
98: [ DMR07 ] to classify these varieties up to
99: isomorphism and homeomorphism (the generating set ( 1.2 )
100: having proved too unwieldy). One motivation for this work arises from
101: the desire to extend this classification to general Schubert varieties of
102: type A. Experience suggests that presentations for I_{w} that are
103: as simple as possible are best for this purpose.
104: The question of finding
105: simple presentations of I_{w} for other root systems appears to
106: have been less studied.

claims.text: The paper formally conjectures minimality of both displayed \(J_v\)-families and records only a finite computer verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
